explanation: `F.p` is fetched outside any call of `F`; inside each call, `b.Q` is judged on the container's chain read in the site's context, so it reads that call's `y`: `5, 9`.
Called as `F.p(0)`, the container `c` has a static `F` above the activated `p`; `F` is not activated on the reader's chain, so reading `Q` is `LocalOnlyProperty`.
The container `{ X = n }` was written inside the first call of `H`; read inside the second call, it needs the first call's activation and is refused.
A root alias `C = F.p` carried into each call reads that call's `y`.
A body of `F` invoked through a call reference reads the captured call's `y`, and `R.Algorithm(F.p, 5)` reads its own call's `y`.
Inside the call, `open p` and the carried `b.Q` both read the call's `y`.
Each recursive call reads the carried container on its own activation: `0 + 1 + 2 + 3`.
The owner walk runs before any open: the root property `X = 9` is found on the walk, so the opened `X` is never consulted.
The prelude is the outermost property level of the walk, so `count` is the builtin, not the opened member; a bare builtin that requires an argument is its own arity error.
Each level consults its own opens after the walk: inside `F` the inner provider wins, at the root the outer one.
Two providers of `X` are legal while no written name reaches that open level with `X`.
